name: Social democracy
summary: Social democracy is the family of parties, from Germany, Austria, Britain, Sweden and the federations that unite them, that seek social justice through democratic means. They keep a market economy but regulate it, build a universal welfare state, back unions and co-determination, tax wealth and favour international cooperation, development aid and arms control. They reject one-party rule and revolution and differ with one another on nuclear power, migration and public ownership.
scope: A family entry answering only what several branches share. Branches read from their own texts: the Socialist International (Frankfurt 1951, Stockholm 1989), the German SPD (Godesberg 1959, Hamburg 2007), the Austrian SPÖ (2018 programme), British Labour (2024 manifesto), the Swedish SAP (2026 election programme; the 2013 party programme could not be opened) and the Party of European Socialists (2024 manifesto, 2011 principles). The SI and PES are federations of parties, not independent branches. Democratic socialism, Third Way, Nordic model and other entries with their own audit are excluded. Single-branch positions are null and opposing branch positions are 0, low.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Godesberg demands treatment for all regardless of means, the SPÖ programme guarantees a publicly and solidarity-financed health system for everyone, Labour pledges the NHS and the PES promises defence of public healthcare.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The SPÖ wants a minimum wage, Labour a genuine living wage with no age bands and the PES decent minimum wages, but none of them sets a 'substantial' rise as a programme aim.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The SI says markets must function as a dynamic mechanism but that the state must regulate them and cannot leave repair to afterwards; Godesberg favours markets only 'wherever free competition really exists'.

public-ownership.rationale: Frankfurt, the SI and Godesberg accept public ownership where needed but not as a general aim (the SI says nationalisation is no sovereign remedy), Labour wants rail in public ownership while Sweden's 2026 programme only bars privatising hospitals.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The SPD (large wealth and inheritances), the SPÖ (inheritance tax as first measure) and the PES (the wealthiest must pay) all call for more tax on the rich; Labour's 2024 text only targets avoidance.

unions-good.rationale: The SI lists the right to form unions among human rights, Godesberg calls free unions the means by which workers become citizens of the economy, Hamburg and the PES treat unions as partners.

property-fundamental.rationale: Godesberg protects private ownership only 'as long as it does not hinder the establishment of social justice' and Hamburg says property carries obligations.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The SI says the state must regulate the market in the interests of the people and Godesberg names containing the power of big business the key task of economic policy; the PES and Labour also call for shaping markets.

cut-welfare.rationale: The SI says economic rights are not benefits for passive individuals but the base of active participation and demands welfare for all; Godesberg, Hamburg and the SPÖ all defend and extend the welfare state.

worker-ownership.rationale: The SI backs self-managed worker cooperatives and Godesberg supports cooperatives, yet both accept private and public enterprises beside them, so collective worker ownership is one option among several.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

strong-leader.rationale: Godesberg makes government responsible to parliament, with separated powers and respect for the opposition, which a leader bypassing institutions would contradict.

state-harmful.rationale: Godesberg gives the state a social function of security and culture, Hamburg a 'preventive' welfare state, and the SI wants democratic regulation by the state.

limit-guns.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

empower-police-military.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

decide-locally.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

rehabilitation.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

traditional-family.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Hamburg supports same-sex civil partnerships and the PES LGBTIQ equality, but the programmes read do not state marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

more-religion-public.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

gradual-change.rationale: The SI calls democratic socialism a continuing process of social and economic democratisation and Godesberg a constant task won by majorities, though they also seek a new economic order.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Labour pledges to reduce net migration and Sweden's 2026 programme keeps a strict migration policy, while Hamburg says immigration enriches and the PES calls managed migration an opportunity.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Frankfurt says absolute national sovereignty must be transcended, Godesberg wants international law backed by executive power and the SI wants a strengthened UN.

free-trade.rationale: The SI says an open world economy can stimulate the South but also brings vulnerability, and the SPÖ and PES tie trade to social standards while Labour seeks targeted agreements.

nation-first.rationale: The SI says democratic socialism cannot be reached in a few countries, Frankfurt says absolute national sovereignty must be transcended, Hamburg calls social democracy internationalist and the SPÖ warns of nationalism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The programmes read stress UN mandates and peacekeeping, but no branch states military intervention for human rights.

open-borders.rationale: No branch programme calls for open borders; they speak of managed migration.

limit-growth.rationale: The SI and Hamburg endorse qualitative growth compatible with the environment, not limits on growth, and Sweden aims for growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The SPÖ calls the climate crisis a question of survival, the PES a green and social deal and Labour a clean-energy mission.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Hamburg and the SPÖ demand nuclear phase-out while Labour and Sweden's 2026 programme back new nuclear.

revolution-justified.rationale: Frankfurt, Godesberg and the SI pursue socialism only by democratic means, and the scholarship (SEP) presents social democracy as taming capitalism through elections, not revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

central-planning.rationale: The SI endorses decentralised market mechanisms and Godesberg says totalitarian control of the economy destroys freedom; Frankfurt rejects handing all economic decisions to central authorities.

socialized-markets.rationale: Programmes accept markets with private, public and cooperative firms alike, so the statement's condition on ownership is neither affirmed nor denied.

land-value-tax.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Hamburg calls for just taxation of large wealth and inheritances and the SPÖ names taxing large inheritances its first and most important measure; the other branches are silent.

basic-income.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The programmes read call for trade rules and open markets for the South, not for tariff protection of domestic industry.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The SI wants public supervision of investment, Godesberg investment control, Labour a state-led industrial strategy with a National Wealth Fund and the PES public investment.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Frankfurt accepts the right to be rewarded by effort and the SI says socialists claim no blueprint for a final fixed society; no branch aims at abolishing wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Frankfurt warns against a rigid corporative system and Godesberg stresses autonomous bargaining, while the SPÖ programme endorses statutory social partnership.

one-party-rule.rationale: Frankfurt says democracy requires more than one party and the right of opposition, Godesberg condemns party dictatorship and the SI makes free choice between alternatives a condition of democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

democracy-best.rationale: The SI calls political democracy an indispensable element of socialism, Frankfurt says socialism can only be achieved through democracy, and Godesberg says it is fought for as the universal form of state.

direct-votes.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

workers-councils.rationale: Frankfurt says economic organisations must not usurp parliament's prerogatives, and Godesberg and the SI rest power on free elections and parliamentary government.

right-to-secede.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

natural-rulers.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

political-violence-never.rationale: The SI condemns violent handling of conflicts within nations but Frankfurt also supports peoples struggling for freedom against dictatorship, so no unconditional rule is stated.

war-builds-character.rationale: The SI says war destroys human life and the basis of social development, and Godesberg demands that war be ruled out as a means of policy.

separate-church-state.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The SI rejects any form of religious fundamentalism and Godesberg says neither state nor party may interfere in matters of conscience.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

military-superiority.rationale: The SI wants military stability at the lowest possible level of defensive weapons and Godesberg ties defence to disarmament.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The SI says cultural diversity enriches societies and demands equal rights for all races and ethnic groups, and Hamburg calls Germany a country of immigration.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Frankfurt describes class struggle under capitalism while Godesberg and Hamburg do not call it history's main driver.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The SI says basic economic, social and cultural equality is essential, and Hamburg wants more equality in income, wealth and power, while also calling distribution by performance just.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

civilizational-union.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The SI makes solidarity a core value of equal weight with freedom and Godesberg subordinates individual interest to the community's.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Godesberg subordinates individual interest to the community's while the SI calls individual rights fundamental and inseparable from social duties.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The programmes treat nature as a basis of life and sustainable development without stating its value apart from humans.

limit-population.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Godesberg and Frankfurt credit industrial progress with the means to end poverty, though the SI warns of irresponsible industrialism.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

human-enhancement.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

restore-past-order.rationale: The SI links social progress to technological progress and says each generation sets its own goals.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

direct-action.rationale: Godesberg wins support by electoral competition and Frankfurt works through free elections, though Hamburg also values movements and civil society.

means-match-ends.rationale: The SI says democracy and human rights are not simply means but the very substance of socialist ends, and Frankfurt that socialism cannot be reached without freedom.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Frankfurt gives basic needs the first claim on distribution yet accepts the right to be rewarded by effort, and Godesberg and Hamburg tie just distribution to performance.

production-for-use.rationale: Frankfurt makes satisfaction of human needs the guiding principle, but the SI in 1989 and Godesberg accept markets and enterprise profit within regulation.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Frankfurt and Godesberg both reject the dictatorship of a party or class and the SI calls communism discredited by Stalinist crimes.

collective-farming.rationale: Godesberg protects family farms and their ownership and Frankfurt calls private agriculture compatible with socialist planning.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

taxation-theft.rationale: Hamburg says those who earn or own more must contribute more, Godesberg wants excess real-estate gains taxed away and the SPÖ builds its programme on progressive taxation of inheritance and wealth.

harm-principle.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Frankfurt gives groups with their own language a right to cultural autonomy and the SI demands rights for organised minorities and equal rights for nations and denominations.

conscription.rationale: The programmes read do not state a position on conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The SI calls democracy and human rights the indispensable mechanism of popular control, with no precedence for exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Hamburg says law, security, education and health must not become mere commodities and Godesberg ties the state to social security.

positive-liberty.rationale: The SI says freedom needs the greatest chance to act on personal goals and freedom from dependence on owners and power-holders, Godesberg turns fundamental rights into social rights and Hamburg ties freedom to equal opportunity.

media-academia-power.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

organic-representation.rationale: Godesberg has parties compete for majority support and warns against organised interests dominating parliaments, and Frankfurt bars unions from usurping parliament.

total-state.rationale: Godesberg resists every totalitarian rule, Frankfurt rejects totalitarian planning and the SI calls for pluralism.

national-rebirth.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Frankfurt rejects every form of imperialism, Godesberg rules out war as a means of policy and the SI demands respect for national sovereignty.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Godesberg says state power derives from the people and the SI requires free elections, which excludes authority resting on personal oaths of loyalty.

bound-labor.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

universal-morality.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

single-common-good.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

revive-national-language.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The SI wants worker participation and joint decision-making, Godesberg extends co-determination to all large enterprises, Hamburg wants parity co-determination and the PES democracy at work.

school-vouchers.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The SI makes full employment a government responsibility and the PES wants room to invest, while Labour calls its fiscal rules non-negotiable.

economic-freedom.rationale: Godesberg values free choice and enterprise while Frankfurt puts economic democracy first; neither states that political freedom depends on economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

national-self-determination.rationale: The SI demands respect for national sovereignty and the right to national self-government, and Godesberg condemns suppression of peoples' self-determination.

force-without-un.rationale: Hamburg allows German missions only with a binding UN mandate and Frankfurt demands strict implementation of the UN Charter.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Frankfurt and Godesberg accept religious and humanist principles equally as grounds for socialists, so reason alone is not made the sole guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

class-collaboration.rationale: Godesberg turns the SPD from a class party to a people's party and seeks co-responsibility, Labour calls for partnership with business and unions and the SPÖ aims to overcome class antagonism, though Frankfurt still describes class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The SI wants the cultural heritage passed on between generations and Frankfurt wants art and science treasures open to all.

dominated-front.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

workers-nation.rationale: The SI says socialism cannot be reached in a few countries alone, Frankfurt calls it international and Hamburg describes social democracy as always internationalist.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The SI demands full equality of men and women in practice, in the family and at work, and the SPÖ opposes direct and indirect discrimination.

ban-interest.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The SI demands equal rights for all races, Frankfurt abolishing discrimination between racial groups, and the SI names apartheid a crime.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Godesberg and the SI treat the democratic state as an instrument that majorities can use for social justice, not merely a tool of the ruling class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The SI wants renewable and decentralised energy and Labour and the PES drive clean energy.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The SI says cultural diversity enriches rather than endangers and that uniformity threatens democracy, while Hamburg and the SPÖ require integration and language learning.

elite-replacement.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

proportional-representation.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

national-mission.rationale: The SI says different cultures develop their own institutional forms of democracy, which runs against one country spreading its own system.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The SI calls inequality between men and women the most pervasive form of oppression in history and the SPÖ treats women's quotas as breaking de facto male quotas.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Labour's ethics commission aims at its Conservative predecessors, not at a shared view of political elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The SI says manipulation of genetic material must be prevented and demands human dignity and individual rights, which a state eugenic policy would violate.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Godesberg gives the state a social function and the SI says the state must regulate the market and not merely repair damage.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The SI says justice means the end of all discrimination and Frankfurt calls for abolishing racial discrimination.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The SI calls equality the expression of the equal value of all human beings, Godesberg rests politics on the dignity of every person and Frankfurt demands equality before the law whatever birth, sex or colour.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The SI says democratic socialism cannot be attained in only a few countries, but no branch demands revolution abroad.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Godesberg says state power derives from the people, Frankfurt calls democracy government by the people and the SI requires free choice between alternatives.

trade-surplus.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

population-transfer.rationale: The SI demands equal rights for all races, ethnic groups and nations and Frankfurt demands equality before the law whatever birth, creed or colour.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Frankfurt says democracy has the right and duty to protect itself against those who exploit it to destroy it, and Godesberg will not tolerate abuse of freedoms for anti-democratic ends.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The SI demands freedom from dependence on owners of the means of production or holders of political power, and Hamburg condemns a society divided into those who command and those commanded.

separated-powers.rationale: Godesberg wants legislature, executive and judiciary to operate separately, the SPÖ names separation of powers a core of representative democracy and the SI requires an independent judiciary.

vanguard-party.rationale: Frankfurt says communists seek the dictatorship of a single party, Godesberg says they exploit conflicts to establish party dictatorship and the SI condemns the crimes of Stalinism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The SI says cultural diversity enriches rather than endangers and Hamburg that immigration enriched Germany, though Sweden's programme links segregation to weakened cohesion.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The SI says individual rights are fundamental and cannot be played off against one another, though Frankfurt lets democracy defend itself against its enemies.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

party-controls-media.rationale: Godesberg says press, radio and television must be independent and safeguarded from pressure groups, and the SI calls pluralism the guarantee of vitality.

party-commands-army.rationale: Godesberg makes government answerable to parliament and the SI separates party and the democratic state, so a ruling party commanding the army has no place.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Frankfurt says absolute national sovereignty must be transcended, the SPÖ and PES want a more social and democratic EU, and Sweden calls the EU its most important arena; Labour does not contradict this.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

clerical-rule.rationale: The SI rejects any religious fundamentalism and Godesberg bars state and party from interfering in matters of conscience.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Godesberg affirms national defence of the free democratic society and Labour, Sweden and Hamburg stay in NATO, which excludes working for their government's defeat.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Godesberg wants cultural life free from sectional control and the SI protects free expression of opinion.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

recall-officials.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Labour's commitment to NATO is unshakeable, Sweden calls NATO membership a gain and Hamburg commits to NATO cooperation.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

people-in-arms.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The SI demands equal rights and opportunities for the different cultures in each society, but other branches say nothing on ranking cultures.

death-penalty.rationale: The SI protects the inalienable right to life and Hamburg demands that the death penalty be outlawed worldwide.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The SI backs education for equality and family-planning information, but no branch text read states school sex education.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

minority-language-support.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The SI says poor-country debt must be written off and Hamburg calls for systematic debt relief for developing countries.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The programmes of the branches read and the SI declarations state no common position on this statement.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The SI demands 0.7 per cent of GNP aid, Godesberg says developing countries have a claim to help, Hamburg commits to 0.7 per cent and Labour to restore it.
